findings.reason: landing §63 as written ("the other two sites import it with no local copy left") leaves a weaker copy beside its own hardened function, so the divergence §60 closed on the presented-commit path reappears; the done-when should enumerate every site (ideally by a test that finds `rev-parse --verify …^{commit}` calls rather than a hand list, the shape §45 and §50 already use).
findings.text: `_resolve_abbreviated_commit` answers the same question as §63's three sites (does this revision name a commit) with weaker checks — no `--end-of-options`, no timeout — and lives in the very file §63 hardens; `routing._base_commit` (reckon/crew/routing.py:2432) is a third site the plan does not list

findings.reason: §62's done-when should name `fleet_supervisor.config_directory` as a second importer of the moved resolver (crew may import from service.py), otherwise it trades a layering inversion for a second copy of the same resolution and §61's "one resolver" claim stays half true.
findings.text: `config_directory` already resolves `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` exactly as `paid_lanes.systemd_user_dir` does, so §62's "neutral module" home for the resolver is not neutral: moving it into `reckon/service.py` leaves two XDG-base resolvers unless `fleet_supervisor` is repointed too

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — no open section adds a new module; §63 consolidates a spread of resolvers into one, which adds depth rather than surface.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §63 undercounts the commit resolvers it plans to leave one of, and §62 adds a third XDG config-home resolver beside an existing one.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the open sections name the files they extend (§62 cites reckon/service.py and reckon/crew/paid_lanes.py; §63 cites the three resolver sites), and §63 exists because a prior review already searched for the duplicate.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §62 relocates existing machinery and §63 extends one owner; neither adds a layer over machinery it declines to extend.
